title: Protected
description:
Some operations should be available to derived classes but not to the outside world. That is what `protected` is for.

`Account`:
- `long long balance() const`
- `bool deposit(long long cents)`: refuses amounts that are not positive
- a **protected** `void adjust(long long cents)` that changes the balance by any amount, no questions asked

`SavingsAccount` (derived from `Account`):
- `explicit SavingsAccount(double yearlyRatePercent)`
- `void addMonthlyInterest()`: adds one twelfth of the yearly rate, in whole cents rounded down, using `adjust`
- `bool withdraw(long long cents)`: allowed at most **3 times** in total; refuses amounts that are not positive or exceed the balance

Outside code must not be able to call `adjust`.
hints: `protected:` members are visible to derived classes but not to outside code, so `SavingsAccount` can call `adjust` and a caller cannot.
Monthly interest in whole cents: `balance() * yearlyRatePercent / 100 / 12`, then convert to `long long`, which rounds down for positive amounts.
